posts.title: Calm can't be forced (quotes)

slides.text: Nobody ever calmed down because someone *told them to*.
Calm isn't a switch you flip. It's what your body does when it finally *feels safe*.
So instead of “calm down”, try this: unclench your jaw. Drop your shoulders. *Breathe out slower than you breathe in.*
Your mind follows your body more often than the other way round.
Be gentle with a nervous system that learned to stay alert. *It was trying to protect you.*
Send this to the friend who keeps being told to relax.

posts.caption:
Calm can't be forced. It can only be invited. 🌿

Which of these do you need today?

Save this for the next time your mind won't slow down.

posts.title: The kettle that was told to calm down (story)

slides.title: The Kettle That Was Told to Calm Down
slides.subtitle: a little story about forcing calm

slides.text: There was once a kettle that whistled loudly every evening.
“Stop that noise!” everyone said. “Just calm down.”
The kettle tried. It held its breath. It only whistled louder.
Because the whistle was never the problem. *The flame underneath was still burning.*
Then someone did something different. They didn't shout. *They turned the flame down.*
Slowly, quietly, the kettle stopped whistling. Nobody had to tell it to.
If you can't calm down, stop shouting at yourself. Find *your flame*: too little sleep, too much on your plate, a worry you haven't said out loud.
Send this to someone whose kettle has been whistling for a while.

posts.caption:
A little story about why “just calm down” never works. 🫖

What's the flame under your kettle this week?

posts.title: Quiet signs you're healing (quotes)

slides.text: Quiet signs you're healing that *nobody claps for*
You pause before you reply, instead of *reacting*.
You rest *without explaining why*.
You notice the old thought, and don't follow it all the way down.
You say no, and the guilt is *smaller than last time*.
You're kinder to the version of you who *didn't know better yet*.
Send this to someone who's doing better than they think.

posts.caption:
Healing is usually quiet. 🌿

Which one have you noticed in yourself lately?

posts.title: The plant that kept being moved (story)

slides.title: The Plant That Kept Being Moved
slides.subtitle: a little story about growing at your own pace

slides.text: A woman brought home a small plant and set it by the window.
A week later, it hadn't grown. “Maybe it needs more sun,” she thought, and moved it.
Another week. Still nothing. She moved it again. And again.
The plant wasn't failing. It was growing *roots*, where nobody could see.
But every time it was moved, its roots had to start over.
So she left it in one place. She watered it. *She waited.*
One morning, there was a new leaf.
Some growth happens underground first. *Stop digging yourself up to check.*
For anyone who feels like nothing is changing yet.

posts.caption:
A little story for the weeks when it feels like nothing is changing. 🌱

Save it for the days you're impatient with yourself.

posts.title: Things I'm slowly unlearning (quotes)

slides.text: Things I'm *slowly* unlearning
That rest is something I have to *earn*.
That my worth goes up and down with how much I got done today.
That if I stop being hard on myself, *I'll stop growing*.
That everyone else's mood is *my job to fix*.
That I have to be fully healed before I deserve *good things*.
Which one are you unlearning too? Tell me in the comments.

posts.caption:
Unlearning is slow, and that's okay. 🌿

Which one are you working on? Tell me below.

posts.title: The phone that never charged (story)

slides.text: There was once a phone that *everyone* needed.
Messages from family. Calls from work. A friend who needed to talk at midnight.
Its battery said 12%. Then 5%. Then 1%.
“I'll charge later,” it said. “Someone might need me.”
Then the screen went dark. And for a while, it couldn't help *anyone at all*.
Here's the thing: nobody feels guilty for *charging their phone*.
Rest isn't you letting people down. *It's how you keep showing up.*
Send this to the person who's always at 1%.

posts.caption:
Nobody feels guilty for charging their phone. 🔋

When did you last charge yourself?

posts.title: A 30-second reset (quotes)

slides.text: A 30-second reset for when everything feels *too much*
*1.* Look around. Name five things you can see.
*2.* Feel your feet on the floor. Press them down, gently.
*3.* Breathe in for 4. Breathe out for 6. Do it twice.
*4.* Open your hands. Let your shoulders drop.
*5.* Ask yourself: what is the *one next thing*? Only that.
Save this for the next hard afternoon.

posts.caption:
Thirty seconds, no app needed. 🌿

Save it, and try it the next time your day gets loud.
